page.layout: One column of verse, set in italic with roman capitals and some roman words; the running head at the top and the page number at the top right. No marginal notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: Turbidos vultus, hilaretque frontem, Candide Lecti.
Quæ ferox cunctos Libitina carpit Quæ Duces æquat tenui superbos Pauperi, votis precibúsque flecti Nescia puris,
Coniugem dulci rapuit marito, Moribus castis, placidis, pudicis: Atque præstanti pietate claram, Flore iuventa.
Illa te pulchra faceret parentem Prole, maturos aperire partus Si Deus magni voluisset orbis Arbiter æquus.
Optimo visum est aliter Parenti, Qui simul sedes superas inire Sanxerat matrem, & genitum latentem Matris in alvo.
Sic piam vita potiore donans Fœminam, nostri quibus advocavit Gaudiis, & quàm recreat suavi Nectaris hauftu.
Illa nunc firmo fruitur favore Numinis: nullos metuit dolorum Impetus: nec dura furentis horret Classica Martis,
Qui fremit toto violentus orbe, Qui rapax latè populatur agros,

page.notes: The first stanza continues from the previous page, so its opening is a fragment. Printed letters that are hard to read: "Quæ" (second line of the verse) and "nostri" are read from the scan with some doubt. Printed "hauftu" is kept as printed; it is probably the printer's spelling for hausto. No other doubtful readings.
